operations.anchor: The eight historical proposals are evidence of earlier intent:
operations.new: App-shell's local AGENTS fixes the priority order as **stability, simplicity, performance**. Before changing session or timeline code, it requires recording a production benchmark baseline and comparing it after the change. Session UI's local AGENTS separately requires i18n keys for production-visible copy, preserves existing English text byte-for-byte during migration and forbids changing English text or keys to facilitate translation. These are attributed maintenance obligations; this L1 correction records them without modifying product code or executing a benchmark. (`A/AGENTS.md:1–4`; `S/AGENTS.md:1–7`.)

operations.anchor: The app adapter wraps the generated client and maps wire results into app view contracts.
operations.new: The generated Client has its own runtime dependency rule: root AGENTS permits Client dependencies on Schema and Protocol and forbids dependencies on Core or Server at runtime. This Client prohibition is distinct from the explicitly permitted `platform:browserSafe` Core-helper exception for the UI layer described above; that UI exception does not authorize a Client runtime dependency. After a public Protocol or Server `HttpApi` change, root AGENTS requires `bun run generate` from `packages/client`; raw `packages/client/src/generated` and `packages/client/src/generated-effect` files must never be hand-edited. These are prescribed change requirements; no Client generation or product change was performed here. (`AGENTS.md:1–2`.)
operations.section: Transport, stream health and canonical recovery

operations.anchor: Core checks an existing ID, rejects a different equivalent payload, publishes the admission event, requires a durable aggregate sequence and finds the projected record before returning.
operations.old: Core checks an existing ID, rejects a different equivalent payload, publishes the admission event, requires a durable aggregate sequence and finds the projected record before returning.
operations.new: Core returns the previous admission when an existing ID has an equivalent session, encoded prompt and delivery; non-equivalent reuse rejects with `LifecycleConflict`. When it creates a new admission, Core publishes the admission event, requires a durable aggregate sequence and finds the projected record before returning.

The local benchmark condition remains specific and mandatory for app-shell session or timeline changes: record a **production benchmark baseline before the change** and **compare it after the change**. The performance directory's normal-run exclusion and the diagnostic interpretation above do not remove that prescribed condition. This documentation correction changes no session/timeline product code and executes no benchmark or product test. (`A/AGENTS.md:1–4`.)
